h1: The 7 Best Monitor Privacy Screens Under $75 for Open Offices, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 monitor privacy screens under $75 compared on viewing angle, mounting, glare control and sizing for 24 and 27 inch displays.
summary: The 27 inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter is the best pick for large displays because it is reversible and sized by visible area, while its 24 inch twin covers the most common office panel. The Vxaop 2-Pack gives a stated 60 degree viewing cone for two monitors, the Magicmoon 2-Pack suits a pair of 24 inch screens, and the SightPro is the straightforward single-filter choice.
intro: The biggest mistake with privacy filters is buying by the monitor's advertised size. A 24 inch panel and a 24 inch filter are not always the same thing, because filters are cut to the visible area, and a few millimetres off leaves either a gap showing the edge of the screen or a film that will not sit in its brackets. Measure first, then shop.

This ranking is built around fit and function rather than hype. We reviewed seven monitor filters from their listings, comparing size match, viewing angle, how they attach, glare handling and whether the pack covers one monitor or two. Where a listing does not state a number, we leave it out instead of guessing.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 27 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: A reversible 27 inch filter that does not black out the view behind you.
products.description:
This filter is made for 16:9 monitors at 27 inches and sits in the $25 to $50 bracket. The listing calls it reversible, which means one side is glossy and the other matte, so you can choose between sharper contrast and lower reflections.

It takes first place because large monitors are where shoulder-surfing is most likely: a 27 inch panel is visible from a wide arc of a cubicle floor. The reversible film gives you a choice that fixed-finish rivals lack. The listing also notes that it does not block visibility directly behind you, so a person standing at your back still sees the screen. That is the honest limit of every filter of this type.

Buy it if you have a 27 inch 16:9 panel and want one well-suited filter. Skip it if you need protection from someone directly behind you, because no film can offer that.
pros: Clear sizing guidance on the listing
cons: Does not block view from directly behind
products.idealFor: Anyone with a 27 inch monitor in a shared workspace.
products.skipIf: Your monitor is not a 27 inch 16:9 panel.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 24 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: The same reversible design, cut for the most common office monitor size.
products.description:
This is the 24 inch version of the top pick, with the same reversible film and the same 16:9 target. It also lands in the $25 to $50 bracket, so the choice between the two comes down to the panel on your desk.

It ranks second only because fewer people with a 24 inch monitor need a single filter than need one cut for a larger screen where privacy risk is higher. Mechanically it is identical, including the limit that someone directly behind you can still read the display. Compared with the two-packs below it is cheaper per unit of effort if you have only one monitor.

It is the right pick for a single 24 inch office monitor. Skip it if you run dual 24 inch screens, because a two-pack costs little more.
pros: Same design as the 27 inch pick
cons: Cannot hide view from behind you
products.idealFor: Single 24 inch monitor users in open offices.
products.skipIf: You have two monitors to cover.

products.name: Vxaop [2-Pack] 27 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter (16:9 Aspect Ratio)
products.verdict: Two 27 inch filters with a stated 60 degree privacy cone and a matte coating.
products.description:
The Vxaop pack ships two 27 inch filters for 16:9 screens. The listing states a 60 degree privacy angle, an anti-glare matte coating and a 95% blue light reduction claim, all at the $25 to $50 bracket.

It ranks third because it gives you the clearest numbers in the group and two filters for a dual setup. A 60 degree cone means the image fades out as you move off axis, which is the core job of the product. The blue light figure is a vendor claim and its benefit for eyes is modest, so do not buy for that. It sits below the single reversible filters because the matte coating cannot be flipped to a glossy side.

Pick it for a pair of 27 inch monitors. Skip it if you want the sharpest possible image, since matte films soften fine text slightly.
products.idealFor: Dual 27 inch setups that need clear privacy numbers.
products.skipIf: You want a glossy finish for sharp images.

products.name: Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Monitor
products.verdict: Two 24 inch filters that darken the screen from side angles for open-plan desks.
products.description:
The Magicmoon pack covers two 24 inch 16:9 monitors and states that the screen appears dark when viewed from the side. It is positioned for open workspaces and sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

It ranks fourth because it matches the Vxaop idea at a smaller size, but the listing offers fewer numbers, with no stated viewing angle. The listing is also explicit that the filter is for 24 inch panels measured diagonally, which is useful clarity about sizing. It beats the other two-pack below on that clear statement.

Buy it for two 24 inch monitors in a shared office. Skip it if you want a documented angle figure before you commit.
products.idealFor: Shared offices with two 24 inch monitors.
products.skipIf: You want a published angle figure.

products.name: [2-Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen 16:9 Aspect Ratio Widescreen Monitor
products.verdict: A micro-louver 24 inch two-pack with published dimensions and simple mounting.
products.description:
This pack uses a micro-louver design, a fine internal slat structure that narrows what can be seen from the side. The listing gives the dimensions as 532 by 299 millimetres for the visible area of a 24 inch panel and includes two simple mounting methods.

It ranks fifth because published dimensions are valuable, since you can check them against your own screen before buying, yet the listing is weaker on stated angle and coating than the Vxaop. It sits $25 to $50 like its rivals. Micro-louver films work well but can leave faint horizontal lines at certain distances, a known tradeoff of the technology.

Buy it if you want to verify the fit with a tape measure first. Skip it if faint louver lines would bother you.
products.idealFor: Careful buyers who measure their screen first.
products.skipIf: You are bothered by visible film texture.

products.name: [2 Pack] Computer Privacy Screen 27 Inch for 16:9 Widescreen Monitor
products.verdict: A two-piece 27 inch set that is handy for a spare or a second display.
products.description:
The Protescreen listing is for two 27 inch filters aimed at 16:9 widescreens, with a pitch about repeated design updates. It is in the $25 to $50 bracket, like the rest of the group.

It ranks sixth because the details are thinner: the listing does not give a viewing angle, coating type or mounting guide that we could carry over. Two filters is the real value, either for dual monitors or as a spare when you scratch the first. It trails the Vxaop, which is the same size and pack count but documents more.

Buy it for a second 27 inch screen on a budget. Skip it if you want clearer specifications.
products.idealFor: Dual 27 inch users who want a spare.
products.skipIf: You prefer documented specs and angles.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A multi-layered 24 inch film with published dimensions, sold as a single piece.
products.description:
The SightPro is a single 24 inch filter with a multi-layered film and a listed visible area of 532 by 299 millimetres. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket and the listing describes it as blacking out the screen for onlookers.

It places last because it is a single filter priced similarly to the two-packs, which makes it the weakest value here. The published dimensions are a plus and match the other 24 inch picks, so fit checking is easy. If you have one monitor and want the simple option, it works.

Buy it for one 24 inch screen when the reversible filter above is out of stock. Skip it if you have two monitors.
cons: Little detail on angle or coating
products.idealFor: Single 24 inch monitor owners wanting simplicity.
products.skipIf: You want better value per filter.

whatMatters.detail: Filters are cut to the visible area of the panel, not the outer bezel. A 24 inch 16:9 screen measures about 532 by 299 millimetres, and listings that publish these numbers make checking easy. Measure the lit area with a tape and compare before you order.

The privacy cone is the angle within which the screen is readable. A narrower cone hides more from bystanders but also dims the image for you if you shift in your seat. A stated figure such as 60 degrees is more useful than the phrase side-blocking.

Matte films reduce reflections but soften fine text slightly, while glossy ones keep contrast. A reversible film, as on the top two picks, lets you try both. Judge by the lighting in your office, since bright windows favour matte.

Filters attach with adhesive strips, clips or sticky tabs. Removable mounting lets you take the filter off for presentations. Check the listing for the mounting type and whether it leaves residue on the bezel.

A filter hides the screen from the sides, not from behind. It also dims the display a little, so you may raise brightness. Think of it as a shield against neighbours rather than a full privacy solution.

faq.q: Will these filters fit a curved or ultrawide monitor?
faq.a: No. Every filter here is cut for a flat 16:9 panel. Curved and ultrawide displays have different dimensions, so look for filters made for your exact aspect ratio.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Ordering by advertised monitor size without checking the visible area. Measure the lit display, then compare with the listed dimensions such as 532 by 299 millimetres for 24 inch panels.

faq.q: Is the reversible filter worth it over a matte two-pack?
faq.a: If you have one monitor and unsure lighting, yes, since you can flip sides to suit the room. If you have two screens, the Vxaop pack costs little more and documents a 60 degree angle.

faq.q: How do I install a privacy filter?
faq.a: Clean the screen, line up the film with the visible area, and attach it with the supplied tabs or strips. Fit it slowly so no dust is trapped, and keep the film flat.

faq.q: How do I clean the film?
faq.a: Use a dry microfibre cloth, or a lightly damp one for smudges. Avoid sprays and alcohol, which can mark coatings and leave streaks.

faq.q: Will it make my screen look dim?
faq.a: Slightly. Privacy films cut light reaching your eyes, so many users raise brightness a notch. Matte versions can also soften small text a little.

finalTake: For a large display, the 27 inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter is the best monitor privacy screen here, with a reversible finish and a clear size match. The 24 inch version is the matching pick for standard office panels, and the Vxaop 2-Pack is the choice for dual 27 inch setups with a stated 60 degree cone. Magicmoon and the micro-louver two-pack serve dual 24 inch desks. Measure your visible screen area before you order.
